title: Catch-up: GPUs, CPUs and RAM, August to November 2026
summary: 2026 has been the year of the memory shortage. AI data centres are buying up DRAM and GDDR, so RAM costs roughly 4-5x what it did in late 2025 and graphics cards sell far above MSRP (about 44% above on average across 10 countries in October). No new GeForce or Radeon gaming GPUs launched this year, and the next big CPU platforms (Intel Nova Lake, AMD Zen 6) slipped into 2027. The first small signs of cooling are showing: DRAM spot prices flattened since late October and the RTX 5090 fell sharply in Europe and Japan.
takeaways: Prices are NOT falling overall yet. GPUs rose about 35% from August to October; RAM is still creeping up, just more slowly.
Biggest drop right now: RTX 5090 in Germany/EU, down about 34% in one week (€8,450 to €5,610, Nov 6-14). Japan's 5090 is also well off its peak.
If you can wait, wait: forecasts see no real RAM relief before late 2027 or 2028, but GPU spikes like the 5090's are already unwinding.
No new gaming GPUs until 2027 (AMD RDNA 5, maybe Nvidia later). Next CPUs: Intel Nova Lake around CES 2027; AMD Zen 6 desktop possibly mid-2027, still on AM5.
Black Friday is Friday 27 November. Watch for real deals on RTX 5070/5070 Ti and RX 9070-class cards, but compare against MSRP.

items.headline: No new GeForce gaming cards in 2026; RTX 50 Super shelved
items.detail: Nvidia skipped CES 2026 GPU launches for the first time in five years. The RTX 50 Super refresh (e.g. a 24GB RTX 5080 Super) was reportedly finished but put on hold because of the memory shortage, and RTX 60 'Rubin' is now expected around 2028. Nvidia reportedly cut GeForce supply by about 20% and prioritised lower-VRAM cards.

sources.title: Tom's Hardware: no new RTX gaming GPUs in 2026 (Feb 5)

items.headline: 24GB RTX 5080 reportedly cancelled
items.detail: 3GB GDDR7 modules reportedly cost about three times more than before, which killed the higher-VRAM 5080 variant (mid-November report).

items.headline: AMD RDNA 5 not before late 2027
items.detail: Leaker Kepler_L2 (Oct 12) says the RDNA 5 reveal is likely in the second half of 2027, Computex 2027 at the earliest. Only one mid-range chip (AT2) would arrive in 2027; the flagship and smaller chips in 2028. Rumoured flagship: up to 96 CUs, GDDR7, 384-bit bus.

items.headline: Radeon price hikes and RX 7000 end of life
items.detail: AMD has raised Radeon GPU and GDDR6 kit prices several times this year, with another hike reported for November. RX 7000 cards have reached end of life and are disappearing from shelves.

sources.title: TechPowerUp: AMD reportedly plans another Radeon price hike for November

items.headline: Intel Arc: Battlemage stays, Celestial gaming cards reportedly cancelled
items.detail: Arc B580/B570 remain Intel's gaming cards. Discrete gaming GPUs for Xe3P 'Celestial' were reportedly cancelled, and a gaming version of next-gen Xe4 'Druid' (late 2027) is uncertain. Arc B580 in the EU jumped from €350 (Oct 30) to about €494 (Nov 14).

sources.title: Tom's Hardware: Intel reportedly cancels Celestial gaming GPUs (Apr 25)

items.headline: RTX 5090 is the most distorted card on the market
items.detail: US lowest price went from $3,500 (Feb) to $6,890 (Sep) to about $9,400 (Oct), 4.7x the $1,999 MSRP. Nvidia says 5090 supply is 'somewhat constrained'. Since then prices have started to fall: Newegg restocked at $6,249.99 and EU prices fell a third in a week.

sources.title: TechSpot via Xenospectrum: GPU prices +11% in a month (Nov 3)

items.headline: Intel Nova Lake (Core Ultra 400) expected very late 2026 / CES 2027
items.detail: New LGA 1954 socket (new motherboards needed). Leaks point to up to 33% faster gaming than Arrow Lake, but the big 52-core and large-cache 'bLLC' gaming versions may not come until around summer 2027. A Nov 5 leak claims clocks are capped at 5.1 GHz above 90°C, so good cooling will matter.

sources.title: Tom's Hardware: Nova Lake 5.1 GHz limit above 90°C leak (Nov 5)
Tom's Hardware: Zen 6 and Nova Lake reportedly delayed to CES 2027 (Feb 21)

items.headline: AMD Zen 6 desktop (Olympic Ridge) slips, possibly past Computex 2027
items.detail: Reportedly moved to TSMC's performance-focused N2X 2nm node; launch could slip to around July-August 2027 (Nov 19 rumour). Good news: it stays on AM5, so current AM5 boards should work.

sources.title: Wccftech: Zen 6 desktop reportedly slips past Computex 2027 (Nov 19)

items.headline: New X3D chips this year: Ryzen 7 9850X3D and Ryzen 9 9950X3D2
items.detail: The 9850X3D (a faster 9800X3D, up to 5.6 GHz) launched at $499. The 9950X3D2 Dual Edition (16 cores, 3D cache on both chiplets, 192 MB L3) launched April 22 at $899 / €910.

items.headline: Intel Arrow Lake refresh is cheap right now
items.detail: Core Ultra 5 250K Plus has dropped below $150 and Core Ultra 7 270K Plus is around $232 in the US (November). CPUs are the one part that isn't badly hit by the shortage, though Intel is reportedly planning ~10% price rises ahead of its next launch.

sources.title: Wccftech: Zen 6 desktop reportedly slips past Computex 2027 (Nov 19)

items.headline: DDR5 costs about 4-5x pre-shortage prices
items.detail: The cheapest 2x16GB DDR5-6000 CL30 kit in the US is about $429 (Nov 16), up from about $95 before the shortage and $390 in July. Average listing about $622. 64GB kits are around $1,360. DDR4 is also up 120-180% in a year.

items.headline: Still rising, but slowing
items.detail: DRAM contract prices rose 93-98% in Q1, 58-63% in Q2, 13-18% in Q3, and are forecast +10-15% in Q4 (TrendForce). Bank of America sees +8% in Q4 and +5% in Q1 2027.

sources.title: Shattered: RAM still climbing as NAND falls 20% (Nov 19)

items.headline: First sign of cooling: DRAM spot prices have flattened
items.detail: DDR4 chip spot prices are down 5.6% from their Oct 26 record, and DDR5 chip spot is flat around $60 since early November. In Shenzhen, 16GB DDR5 modules are trading below contract prices. Spot usually leads retail by a few months.

sources.title: Shattered: RAM still climbing as NAND falls 20% (Nov 19)

items.headline: SSDs may get cheaper first
items.detail: NAND flash spot prices fell about 20% since mid-October. Consumer NAND contract prices are expected to fall in Q1-Q2 2027, though retail SSD cuts haven't shown up yet.

sources.title: Shattered: RAM still climbing as NAND falls 20% (Nov 19)

items.headline: Relief not expected before late 2027 or 2028
items.detail: Micron says over 75% of its 2027 DRAM output is already sold; SK hynix has long-term deals covering more than half of 2027-28 capacity. Counterpoint sees the earliest turn in Q4 2027; Gartner 'late 2027'; Intel's CEO says 2028.

items.headline: Nvidia's gaming business is still growing despite the shortage
items.detail: Nvidia's graphics segment revenue was $7.92B in Q2 of fiscal 2027, up 46% year over year, though it doesn't break out GeForce alone. The company says RTX 5090 supply is 'somewhat constrained' while AI chips get priority for memory.

sources.title: TechSpot via Xenospectrum: GPU prices +11% in a month (Nov 3)

items.headline: Jensen Huang resigned on Nov 12, then was reinstated on Nov 23
items.detail: Huang stepped down on Nov 12 amid reports of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, and CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO. Reports also said the board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a possible successor. On Nov 23 the board unanimously reinstated Huang after input from the US government; investigations by an independent committee, the SEC and the DOJ continue.

sources.title: Al Jazeera: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO (Nov 23)

items.headline: Memory makers are sold out into 2027-28
items.detail: Micron says over 75% of its 2027 DRAM output is already sold, and SK hynix has long-term deals covering more than half of 2027-28 capacity. Team Group's CEO sees 'no downward price trend' in 2027. AI data centres are the reason.

trends.note: Lowest in-stock prices: RTX 5080 $2,260 (MSRP $999), 5070 Ti $1,459, 5070 $900, RX 9070 XT $980 (Nov 23).
RTX 5090 fell sharply (Nov 6-14), but RTX 5060 Ti 16GB (+14%), RX 9060 XT 16GB (+13%) and RTX 5080 (+€100) rose.
RTX 5080 £1,640, 5070 Ti £1,299, 5070 £780, RX 9070 XT £830, RX 9070 £750 (Nov 23). Little week-to-week history yet.
RTX 5090 ¥1,198,000 (Nov 3) vs about ¥1.48M at the October peak. RTX 5080 ¥331,800, 5070 Ti ¥230,800.
Cheapest 32GB DDR5-6000 kit $429 (Nov 16) vs $420 (Oct 30). Slow climb.
German DDR5 retail prices are over 5x mid-2025 levels.
Premium 32GB kits hit £1,199.99 at Overclockers UK in August; new stock is priced well above old stock.
DRAM spot prices have stopped rising since late October; contract prices still up 10-15% this quarter.
Arrow Lake Plus chips at record lows (250K Plus < $150). AMD X3D chips holding near MSRP.

alerts.note: Nov 6 to Nov 14. Still far above the ~€2,300 launch price.
